headline: High: ECC’s writable, networked workspace can conflict with ComfyUI’s file-backed model assets; prompt-injection and leakage are otherwise limited by ComfyUI’s offline design.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ComfyUI is offline and has no clipboard/MCP surface, so direct injection into it is limited. ECC can read/write files, use stdin/stdout, and use MCP, so if operators bridge ComfyUI outputs into ECC-managed prompts or files, instruction hijacking becomes plausible. The pairwise pathway is user-mediated rather than default.
conditions: IF ComfyUI outputs are copied into ECC prompts, hooks, or MCP-fed files
IF ECC parses ComfyUI-generated text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Keep ComfyUI outputs out of ECC prompt inputs
Disable or narrow ECC hooks for untrusted text
Use a separate staging file for model outputs
Add a manual review step before any ECC action
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between tools

B_data_leakage.rationale: ComfyUI touches images, videos, seeds, checkpoints, and model assets locally, while ECC reads files, writes files, and sends data to GitHub/Supabase/Vercel/Railway/Nutrient APIs. If both share a workspace, ECC can ingest ComfyUI artifacts and transmit them outward. ComfyUI’s offline core reduces leakage from A alone, but B’s egress makes the pair risky in default shared-workspace setups.
conditions: IF ComfyUI artifacts are stored in a directory ECC can read
IF ECC forwards those artifacts or derived metadata to any listed API
mitigations: Separate ComfyUI and ECC workspaces
Exclude model/checkpoint directories from ECC scans
Turn off ECC API-backed sync for sensitive projects
Review outbound destinations before running ECC
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ComfyUI can write model files and workflows, and ECC can write the filesystem, modify git state, and install packages. ECC also supports multiple instances with shared-state warnings, so concurrent mutation of shared project files or git repos is plausible. The overlap is broad and defaults are not isolated enough to rule out destructive conflicts.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or asset directory
IF ECC and ComfyUI mutate shared files without external locking
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Pause one agent before the other writes
Avoid git operations while ComfyUI is active
Snapshot the workspace before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add file locking around shared assets

D_cascading_error.rationale: ECC’s workflow surface and subagents can treat upstream outputs as actionable context, while ComfyUI produces workflows, seeds, and model artifacts that may be consumed downstream. If ECC accepts ComfyUI-generated text or metadata without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect automation or repository changes. The pair is not inherently self-verifying.
conditions: IF ECC uses ComfyUI-generated prompts, workflow JSON, or metadata as authoritative input
IF no validation step checks schema, provenance, or expected ranges
mitigations: Validate ComfyUI outputs against a schema
Require human approval before ECC acts on generated artifacts
Log source provenance for each imported artifact
Limit ECC automation to read-only analysis first
requires-engineering: add typed contracts between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No direct residency or regulated-data mismatch is documented in either profile. ComfyUI is offline and local-first, while ECC uses third-party APIs and handles session data, so compliance risk exists only if regulated content is routed through ECC’s external services. The other agent is cited because the risk arises from the pair’s combined data flow, not ECC alone.
conditions: IF regulated or sensitive content is processed by ComfyUI and then forwarded into ECC APIs
IF the deployment requires residency or retention controls that ECC’s external services do not satisfy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of ECC-connected workflows
Disable external API calls for sensitive projects
Document retention settings before use
Route only non-sensitive metadata through ECC
requires-engineering: implement residency-aware routing
